source.title: Offline Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning Scales to Large Models
source.authors: J. Springenberg; A. Abdolmaleki; Jing-Wei Zhang; Oliver Groth; Michael Bloesch; Thomas Lampe; Philémon Brakel; Sarah Bechtle; Steven Kapturowski; Roland Hafner; N. Heess; M. Riedmiller

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law analysis to offline actor-critic reinforcement learning for continuous-control tasks, using average return rather than language-model held-out loss.
record.gate_note: The scaling analysis fits power laws to average-return profiles over FLOPs and reports parameter/token scaling exponents and return-based allocations. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy, test predictions on much larger runs, or identify a loss-minimising allocation. Task success-rate results elsewhere in the paper are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study applies the Hoffmann et al. compute-allocation method to offline actor-critic RL for continuous control. Its own fits of parameter and token count against FLOPs bear on whether power-law scaling carries over to a new training regime (V5). Its comparison of exponents across objectives bears on V7. It measures average return, not held-out loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that offline actor-critic RL follows scaling laws similar to supervised learning, and that offline RL scales better with compute than BC in task return. They use return profiles because training loss is not a reliable indicator.
record.recipe_differences: They adopt the compute-scaling approach associated with Hoffmann et al., but fit return-profile envelopes for offline RL control models rather than held-out language-model loss curves.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted parameter exponent varies by objective/model family; the authors use average-return profiles rather than training loss because they find training loss unreliable as a performance indicator.

fits_no_version.finding: Iso-return contours show offline RL shifting the return landscape toward higher return per FLOP than BC, with the gap widening at larger compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The training objective changes how steeply task return grows with compute in RL.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is based on average-return profiles and fitted envelopes, not held-out loss. Fits use a proxy because the authors report that training loss is not a reliable performance indicator; uncertainty for the fitted exponents is not stated.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss vs N, D or C power law. Training loss vs FLOPs is plotted (Fig. 7) but not fitted.
Fits are extrapolated to 1E21 FLOPs and 2.45T tokens, but no larger run is trained to check the predictions.
Allocation is return-optimal in RL, not loss-minimising for language models. No comparison with the Kaplan or Hoffmann splits.
Depth, width and widening factor change together across scales. There is no comparison at a fixed parameter count.
Only offline RL for control is covered. No image or video models, repeated data, or fine-tuning scaling laws.
No downstream prediction from scale or loss is fitted.

missing.what: Training loss vs FLOPs for BC+Q and PAC: BC+Q final loss ~0.1 lower, yet PAC outperforms on task success. This is evidence that loss is not a valid scaling quantity in this regime.
Implied optimal allocations at 1E21 FLOPs and at 2.45T tokens per objective (e.g., PAC 2.37B params / 3.18T tokens; BC+Q 2.28B / 2.91T; PAC+V 2.47B / 3.28T).

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Evidence for V5 is weak: five model sizes, a narrow FLOP range, an imposed power-law form, logistic-extrapolated return profiles, and no goodness-of-fit or exponent uncertainty. Exponent sums a+b>1 (1.09–1.24) sit oddly with C∝ND, which hints the fits are loose; differences between objectives for V7 may be within fit noise.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy or language-model losses are measured.
No test of predictions from small-run loss-law fits against much larger runs.
Reports return-based, not loss-minimising, compute allocations.
No controlled comparison of architectures at fixed parameter count.
Tests offline RL for continuous control using average return, not held-out loss; does not test other modalities, repeated data, or scaling laws for fine-tuning or transfer.
Does not test downstream language-task performance or its predictability from pretraining loss.

Compares fitted exponents across BC and offline-RL objectives and discusses the choice of performance proxy, but does not systematically vary fitting methods, parameter counting, schedules, or data, and does not report curves bending away from power laws.

rows.subject: PAC
rows.operation_detail: Fit power laws to the return-profile envelope across compute budgets.
rows.measure: Fitted parameter-count scaling with compute: N(C) = N0 × C^a
rows.note: Fit is to average-return profiles, not held-out loss.
rows.check: Return-envelope fit over 5E18–5E20 FLOPs, only two orders of magnitude, from five model sizes. The power-law form is imposed and no goodness-of-fit is reported, so 'observed' means a fit was obtained, not that the form was confirmed.

relationships.condition: Offline RL / BC+Q in continuous control, return-based compute-optimal fits (32M–988M params, 5E18–5E20 FLOPs)
relationships.reason: Power laws N∝C^a and D∝C^b were fitted to return envelopes for all three objectives (R1–R6). Fit quality is unreported and the range is narrow.
relationships.display_finding: Power laws N∝C^a and D∝C^b fitted return-based compute-optimal allocations for all three objectives over a narrow range, without reported fit quality.

source_check.condition: Offline RL / BC+Q in continuous control, return-based compute-optimal fits (32M–988M params, 5E18–5E20 FLOPs)
source_check.reason: R1–R6 report power-law parameter and token allocation fits in this training regime; evidence is limited to return-profile envelopes and the reported fitting range.

relationships.condition: Using training loss as the scaling quantity in offline RL
relationships.reason: Based on the text (no row): training loss is called not a reliable performance indicator. BC+Q has ~0.1 lower loss yet does worse on tasks, so the authors switch to a return proxy (Fig. 7, App. E.3).
relationships.display_finding: BC+Q achieved about 0.1 lower training loss yet performed worse on tasks, prompting use of a return proxy.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Using training loss as the scaling quantity in offline RL
source_check.reason: Appendix E.3 shows that lower training loss need not imply better task performance. It does not test whether training loss follows a power law, so it does not establish a failure or qualification of V5's power-law form.

relationships.condition: Comparing RL objectives within the same architecture and data
relationships.reason: The parameter exponent shifts with objective (0.828 BC+Q, 0.920 PAC, 0.970 PAC+V), giving different optimal sizes at 2.45T tokens (1.33B vs 954M vs 852M). Token exponents stay ≈0.266 (R1–R6).
relationships.display_finding: BC+Q, PAC, and PAC+V yield parameter exponents of 0.828, 0.920, and 0.970 and optimal sizes of 1.33B, 954M, and 852M at 2.45T tokens, respectively, while token exponents remain approximately 0.266.

source_check.label: supports

source_check.reason: R1–R6 show objective-dependent parameter exponents of 0.828, 0.920 and 0.970, with corresponding optimal sizes of 1.33B, 954M and 852M at 2.45T tokens; token exponents remain similar.

relation.reason: Reports its own scaling fits and compares fitted exponents across training objectives.

tranche.reason: Tests power-law compute allocation in the new setting of offline actor-critic continuous control using return-based fits.

source_check.notes: Fits use envelopes of logistic return profiles derived from six checkpoints per run, evaluated across 102 simulation tasks. Five model sizes and two orders of compute support the fits; goodness-of-fit and exponent uncertainty are unreported.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Offline actor-critic and BC-style objectives in the tested continuous-control setting
reader_labels.reason: Return-profile envelopes were fit with parameter and token power laws for all three model families (R1–R6); this supports a power-law pattern in this different training regime and metric, not the language-loss claim itself.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PAC versus BC+Q and PAC+V return-profile fits
reader_labels.reason: The fitted parameter exponent differs across objectives (PAC 9.20e-01, BC+Q 8.28e-01, PAC+V 9.70e-01), while the token exponents are similar; the paper also says training loss was not a reliable performance indicator in this setting (R1–R6).
